title: South Carolina Sales Tax: Rates, Compliance, and Regulations for Businesses
summary: This guide to South Carolina sales tax goes over rates and how their tax system works so you avoid paying penalties due to incorrect filings.
body_markdown:
## South Carolina sales tax at a glance


State taxing authority South Carolina Department of Revenue


South Carolina sales tax rate 6%


Local tax rates 0% to 3%


Combined sales tax rate range 6% to 9%


Economic nexus threshold More than $100,000 in gross revenue during the current or previous calendar year


Website[dor.sc.gov](https://dor.sc.gov/)


Tax line 844-898-8542


South Carolina has a state sales tax rate of 6%. Counties and municipalities have local sales tax rates ranging from 0% to 3%, bringing the combined rate to 6% to 9%.


General retail goods, prepared food, and most SaaS and streaming services are taxable. Downloaded digital products generally aren't. Most groceries are exempt from South Carolina state sales tax, although they may be subject to local sales tax.


Businesses without a physical presence in South Carolina must start collecting and remitting sales tax when they exceed[$100,000 in gross revenue](https://dor.sc.gov/sales-use-tax-index/sales-tax/remote-sellers) from tangible personal property, digital products, or taxable services during the current or previous calendar year.


Once you reach[nexus in South Carolina](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/south-carolina) , you’ll need to register for a Retail License through the South Carolina Department of Revenue. Most businesses are required to file and pay monthly. You can pay online through MyDORWAY, pay with ACH credit, or pay with a paper check.

## South Carolina sales tax rates and calculations


South Carolina sales tax rates range from 6% to 9%. This is based on a statewide base rate of 6% plus local sales tax rates of 0% to 3%.


### List of local sales tax rates in South Carolina


Many cities and counties in South Carolina charge local tax rates on top of the base state sales tax. South Carolina has several types of voter-approved local taxes, including local option, capital projects, transportation, school district, and tourism development taxes.


Each county or city can have a different combination, so they don't follow a simple county-plus-city structure.


Not all municipalities in South Carolina charge local sales taxes, and the exact local tax rates can vary by jurisdiction, zip code, and exact address. Check the chart of[sales tax rates by municipality](https://dor.sc.gov/sites/dor/files/forms/ST575.pdf) before applying tax to a sale.


Here are local tax rates in notable cities and counties across South Carolina:

Charleston Charleston, Berkeley 3% 9%

Columbia Richland 2% 8%

### How to calculate South Carolina sales tax


To calculate the South Carolina sales tax rate, add the base state rate of 6% to the local rate in the applicable municipality. Multiply the total by the purchase price to calculate the sales tax due.


For example, if your sale happens in Charleston County, your combined sales tax rate is 9%. This consists of the 6% state rate and 3% in local taxes. If the purchase price of your item is $50, the sales tax is $4.50 ($50 x 0.09).


### Origin-based vs. destination-based sourcing in South Carolina


South Carolina uses destination-based sourcing to calculate sales tax rates.


Destination-based sourcing means that sales tax rates are calculated based on the buyer’s location, not the seller’s location. It’s most applicable when a buyer makes an online purchase from a seller in a different city or county within South Carolina.


Say your business is located in Charleston County, but your customer is located in Lexington County. The customer pays Lexington County’s combined sales tax rate of 7%, even though Charleston County’s combined sales tax rate is 9%.


### Is South Carolina a Streamlined Sales Tax state?


No. South Carolina isn't a member of the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement. You can't register for a Retail License through the Streamlined Sales Tax Registration System. You must apply and file using the South Carolina Department of Revenue’s[MyDORWAY system](https://mydorway.dor.sc.gov/_/#2) .


## Sales tax nexus in South Carolina


[Nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) means you have enough connections with a state that the state can require you to collect sales tax on its behalf.


Before 2018, states could only require sellers with a physical presence in the state to collect sales tax. In[South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.](https://www.numeral.com/blog/south-dakota-v-wayfair) , the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that rule, and states with a sales tax began setting nexus thresholds.


There are four types of sales tax nexus:


- **Physical:** Your business has a physical presence in the state, such as an office, warehouse, or retail store. Remote employees working from a state also establish a physical nexus.
- **Economic:** Your business reaches a specific sales or transaction volume during a set time period, usually a calendar year.
- **Affiliate:** Your business has an established relationship with another business in the state, such as a partnership or subsidiary.
- **Marketplace:** Your business operates an online marketplace, like Amazon, that facilitates sales for third-party sellers.


Sales tax nexus works differently in every state. Here are the[South Carolina nexus thresholds](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/south-carolina) :


Nexus Type Threshold


[Physical](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) Any physical presence in South Carolina, including stores, offices, inventory storage, or remote employees, even if you don’t meet the economic nexus threshold.
Physical-nexus sellers must start collecting on the date nexus begins. There’s no grace period.


[Economic](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) Gross revenue from sales delivered into South Carolina above $100,000 in the previous or current calendar year.
There is no transaction-count threshold.


Affiliate Out-of-state sellers have nexus if they’re affiliated with a South Carolina business that either sells similar products under the same name, logo, or trademark, or accepts returns, takes orders, provides customer service, or distributes advertising for them.
The out-of-state seller is treated as if it has a physical presence and must collect and remit sales tax.


Marketplace[Marketplace facilitators](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) with gross revenue over $100,000 in South Carolina must collect and remit sales tax on all sales made through their platform, including sales by third-party sellers.
Those sales still count toward each seller’s own $100,000 threshold, but the seller doesn’t remit tax on them.


If you sell products or services in South Carolina, you need to know when you cross the nexus thresholds, so you’re ready to collect and remit on time. You have until the first day of the second month after you cross the economic nexus threshold to register and start collecting sales tax.


Numeral’s[free nexus tracking](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) alerts you as you approach the nexus threshold, so you never miss a filing deadline.


### What’s taxable and exempt in South Carolina


Most tangible personal property is subject to sales tax in South Carolina. Taxability for other items, like groceries and digital products, varies by item and local sales tax rules.


Category Generally Taxable? Additional Information


Tangible personal property Yes Most physical goods are taxable unless specifically exempt


Groceries Varies Most groceries are exempt from the 6% statewide sales tax but may be subject to local sales taxes


Clothing Yes Many clothing items are exempt from sales tax during the state’s annual[tax-free weekend](https://dor.sc.gov/communications/tax-free-weekend) in August but are otherwise generally taxable


Prescription drugs No Most prescription drugs and some other medical supplies are exempt from state sales tax


SaaS Yes Most SaaS platforms and cloud-based software are treated as taxable communications services rather than products


Digital goods Varies Downloaded items like e-books and music files are generally not taxable because they are not tangible, but many software programs and streaming services are treated as communications services and are taxable


Services Varies Some specific services, like communications, utilities, laundry, and accommodations, are taxable, while many others are not


Shipping Varies Shipping taxability varies depending on how the item is transported


### What’s subject to sales tax in South Carolina


State sales tax in South Carolina generally applies to:


- **Tangible personal property:** Most physical items are taxable in South Carolina, including clothing, furniture, toiletries, and electronics.
- **Prepared foods:** Hot prepared foods from restaurants, food trucks, and buffets are subject to state sales tax.
- **Select services:** South Carolina taxes some service categories, including communications, utilities, and laundry. Most other services are tax-exempt.
- **Accommodations:** Hotels and other short-term lodging are subject to state sales tax. The base sales tax rate for accommodations in South Carolina is 7%, which is higher than the general state tax rate of 6%. Some municipalities also have different local tax rates for accommodations.


### What’s exempt from sales tax in South Carolina


South Carolina has a few exemptions to state sales tax, including:


- **Groceries:** Most unprepared grocery items are exempt from state sales tax, although some South Carolina municipalities charge local taxes on them.
- **Prescription medication:** Prescription medication is generally exempt from sales tax, although over-the-counter medication is taxable.
- **Medical equipment:** Most medical equipment and supplies are exempt from state sales tax.
- **Most general services:** While a few service categories are taxable in South Carolina, most are exempt.


### SaaS and digital goods taxability in South Carolina


Sales tax for SaaS and digital goods is treated differently in South Carolina than it is in many other states.


Most[SaaS is taxable in South Carolina](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-south-carolina) because it is treated as communications services. This includes both B2B cloud-based software and B2C platforms like streaming services.


Physical software discs are also taxable because they are considered tangible personal property.


[Software](https://dor.sc.gov/sales-use-tax-software) delivered only electronically, and many other[digital goods](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) , such as downloadable e-books, music, movies, and games, are not taxable. That’s because they are not considered to be tangible personal property or a taxable service.


### Resale and exemption certificates in South Carolina


South Carolina offers[resale certificates](https://www.numeral.com/blog/resale-certificates) , which allow retailers to purchase tangible personal property tax-free as inventory to resell or lease to customers.


To buy inventory tax-free for resale, you must give the seller a completed[Form ST-8A](https://dor.sc.gov/sites/dor/files/forms/ST8A.pdf) , Resale Certificate. You'll need a valid South Carolina Retail License number (or a retail license number from another state).


South Carolina accepts out-of-state resale certifications and[Multistate Tax Commission resale certificates](https://www.mtc.gov/resources/uniform-sales-use-tax-exemption-certificate/) for tax exemptions. Since South Carolina is not a Streamlined Sales Tax state, the state government generally doesn’t accept SST resale certificates.


Retailers should submit their completed ST-8A form directly to the vendor they’re purchasing from, not to the South Carolina Department of Revenue. These resale certificates do not expire, but retailers must keep their South Carolina Retail License active.


Sellers must keep a copy of each certificate to support the exemption in an audit. SCDOR requires you to keep records for[at least four years](https://dor.sc.gov/sites/dor/files/Documents/Policy%20Manuals/Chapter%2023%20-%20Frequently%20Asked%20Questions.pdf) after the return was filed or due.


## Registering for a South Carolina Retail License


To collect sales taxes in South Carolina, you’ll first need to obtain a Retail License and set up a business tax account through the state’s Department of Revenue. You can do this through[MyDORWAY](https://mydorway.dor.sc.gov/_/) , which is the state’s online tax payment portal.


To do this, you’ll need to provide the following information:


- Federal identification number (EIN or SSN)
- Business address
- Business structure
- Details about your business’s owner, officers, and operations
- NAICS code


A South Carolina Retail License requires a one-time $50 fee and is usually processed within five days after submitting an online application.


When your license is approved and your business tax account is set up, you will be assigned a filing frequency based on your business’s earnings and tax liability. Most businesses in South Carolina file monthly, but some file quarterly or annually.


Both state and local sales tax are processed through MyDORWAY.


Once approved, South Carolina Retail Licenses don't expire. However, each license covers one location, so you'll need a new license if your business moves or changes ownership, and a separate license for each location.


Depending on where your business operates in South Carolina, you may also need to obtain a local business license from your county or city government.

### Registration requirements for remote sellers


[Remote sellers in South Carolina](https://dor.sc.gov/sales-use-tax-index/sales-tax/remote-sellers) must start collecting and remitting sales tax once they’ve reached the state’s economic nexus, which is $100,000 in gross in-state revenue during the current or previous calendar year.


Once you exceed the threshold, you must get a Retail License and start collecting and remitting tax by the first day of the second calendar month after you established nexus. For example, if you cross the threshold in March, you must start by May 1.


The registration process for remote sellers is similar to the process for in-state sellers. You’ll need to obtain a Retail License and set up a business tax account through[MyDORWAY](https://mydorway.dor.sc.gov/_/) . During the registration process, be sure to specify that you are a remote seller.


## Collecting South Carolina sales tax


Once you’ve obtained the proper licenses and set up your business tax account, it’s time to start collecting sales taxes from your customers in South Carolina.


Here’s how to collect South Carolina state sales tax, step-by-step:


- **Step 1: Determine if the transaction is taxable.** If South Carolina has an exemption for the product or service you’re selling, sales tax does not apply. Otherwise, the transaction is taxable, and you can move on to the next step.
- **Step 2: Identify the customer’s location.** South Carolina uses destination-based sourcing for remote purchases, so the combined tax rate is based on the customer’s municipality. For in-person purchases, the tax rate is based on your store’s location.
- **Step 3: Apply the correct combined tax rate.** Apply South Carolina’s base sales tax rate of 6%, plus their local tax rate.
- **Step 4: Collect the tax from the customer.** Set up your e-commerce site or POS system to collect South Carolina sales tax automatically.
- **Step 5: Track your collected sales taxes.**[Numeral](https://www.numeral.com/) helps you track the sales tax you’ve collected in each state to make filing easy.


### Marketplace sales


In South Carolina,[marketplace platforms](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) like Amazon, eBay, or Etsy collect and remit sales taxes on behalf of their sellers. If you only sell on a marketplace platform, you won’t need to obtain a South Carolina Retail License or set up a South Carolina sales tax account.


However, if you also sell directly through your own website or another channel, you may need to collect sales tax on those sales yourself. Your marketplace sales count toward South Carolina's $100,000 threshold even though the marketplace collects the tax on them.


If your total sales into the state go over $100,000, you'll need a Retail License and must collect and remit tax on your direct sales, even if those direct sales alone are well under the threshold.


### Shipping and delivery charges


Whether or not to[charge sales tax on shipping](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-shipping) is handled differently by each state.


In South Carolina, taxability for shipping and delivery charges[varies](https://dor.sc.gov/sales-use-tax-delivery-charges) based on how the item is delivered. In most cases, shipping and delivery fees are taxable as long as the product being shipped is also taxable.


Notably, these fees are taxable if you’re shipping the product with your own vehicles, or with a common carrier and the sale is made Free on Board (FOB) at the point of destination. This means the buyer does not assume ownership of the item until it arrives at their location.


However, these fees are not taxable if you are shipping an item with a common carrier and the sale is made FOB at the point of origin. This means the buyer takes ownership of the goods as soon as the carrier loads them.


## Filing and paying South Carolina sales tax


In South Carolina, the[sales tax due date](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-due-dates) is the 20th of the month following the reporting period. If the 20th is on a weekend or state holiday, taxes are due on the next business day. Local sales taxes are included in your South Carolina return and not filed separately.


The easiest way to file South Carolina sales tax is online through[MyDORWAY](https://mydorway.dor.sc.gov/_/) . However, you can also file and pay electronically with some third-party tax software programs. If your tax liability is less than $15,000 per filing period, you also have the option to use a paper form.


According to South Carolina’s[ST-3 Instructions](https://dor.sc.gov/sites/dor/files/forms/ST3I.pdf) , most businesses must file state sales tax monthly. However, some businesses may qualify for less frequent filing schedules based on their sales tax liability.


Filing Frequency Sales Tax Liability


Monthly Default for most businesses


Quarterly Generally, total tax due (state and local) of $100 or less per month, with SCDOR approval


Annually With SCDOR approval


Sales tax returns are considered late if they are not transmitted or postmarked by the 20th of the month.


If you do not have any sales tax due in South Carolina, you still need to file a return once you’ve reached nexus. When filing online, select the zero-sales option.


If you file and pay on time, you can take a discount of 3% of the tax due if it's under $100, or 2% if it's $100 or more. The discount is capped at $3,000 per fiscal year (July 1 to June 30), or $3,100 if you file and pay electronically.


### Filing South Carolina sales tax online


[Filing South Carolina sales tax online](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-south-carolina-sales-tax-online) is straightforward. You can register, file, and pay through the MyDORWAY portal.


After creating an account, you’ll file using a simple online form. You can pay by credit card, ACH debit, or electronic funds withdrawal.


## South Carolina sales tax penalties and interest


South Carolina imposes penalties for late filing and late payments. The penalty for failing to file is 5% of the amount due for each month the filing is late. The penalty for failing to pay is 0.5% of the amount due for each month the payment is late.


Both penalties are capped at 25% of the amount due.


These penalties also come with interest. Interest follows the federal underpayment rate in the Internal Revenue Code, changes quarterly, and compounds daily. As of the fourth quarter of 2026, the rate is[7% a year](https://dor.sc.gov/administrative-interest-penalties-waivers-interest-rate-154) .


## South Carolina sales tax recordkeeping and audits


The South Carolina Department of Revenue (SCDOR) may[audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) your sales tax filings and payments for accuracy. During an audit, the SCDOR will look at reported sales, tax rates, tax collected and paid, and any exemptions to make sure everything was reported correctly.


Here are the documents you should keep on hand, so you’re prepared in the event of an audit:


- Sales records
- Invoices and receipts
- Copies of South Carolina state tax filings
- South Carolina Retail License
- Form ST-8A exemption certificates, if applicable


South Carolina requires businesses to keep these records for at least four years after the return was filed or due, whichever is later. Many businesses err on the side of caution and keep records for seven years or more.


If you want to[appeal an audit](https://dor.sc.gov/notices-compliance/appeals-process) , you can do so by filing a written protest within 90 days of the assessment notice. The fastest way to do this is by completing form C-245 through MyDORWAY, although you can also submit a paper form.

## South Carolina sales tax FAQs


**What is the sales tax rate in South Carolina?** The state sales tax rate in South Carolina is 6%. Local tax rates in South Carolina range from 0% to 3%, bringing the combined tax rate to 6% to 9%.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in South Carolina?** The economic nexus threshold in South Carolina is $100,000 in gross revenue during the current or previous calendar year.


**Is SaaS taxable in South Carolina?** In most cases, yes. In South Carolina, SaaS and other cloud-based platforms are treated as taxable communications services.


**Do marketplace sellers need to collect sales tax in South Carolina?** Generally, no. In South Carolina, marketplace facilitators are responsible for collecting and remitting taxes on behalf of their sellers. In fact, if you only sell on a marketplace platform, you won’t need to obtain a South Carolina Retail License or set up a sales tax account.


**How often do businesses need to file state sales tax returns in South Carolina?** Most businesses need to file state tax returns and make payments monthly.
